## Circular to Intermediaries 1 Acting as Sponsors

## Increase in the minimum paid-up share capital requirement for sponsors

Intermediaries  acting  as  sponsors  are  reminded  that  the  provisions  of  the  Securities  and Futures (Financial Resources) Rules ('FRR') concerning the minimum paid-up share capital requirements that must be observed by corporations that have been licensed to carry on Type 6  regulated  activity  (advising  on  corporate  finance),  have  been  amended.  The  amended provisions will come into force on 1 August 2007 2 .

These  amendments  will  have  the  effect  of  imposing  a  formal  legal  obligation  upon  such licensed corporations at all times to maintain a paid-up share capital of not less than HK$10 million  if  their  licences  are  not  subject  to  the  'no  sponsor  work  licensing  condition'.  The coming into force of these amendments to the FRR on 1 August 2007, was foreshadowed in the Guidelines for Sponsors and Compliance Advisers ('Sponsor Guidelines') which came act as sponsors will be in breach of the FRR if  they  do  not  have  in  place,  and  maintain,  the  minimum  paid-up  share  capital  of  HK$10 million with effect from 1 August 2007.

This new requirement applies only to intermediaries acting as sponsors. Intermediaries that are  subject  to  the  'no  sponsor  work  licensing  condition'  will  not  be  affected  by  the amendments to the FRR and will continue to be required to maintain a minimum paid-up share capital of HK$5 million.

For more information on the sponsor regime, please refer to the Sponsor Guidelines and the Frequently Asked Questions on the SFC website (http://www.sfc.hk). Should you have any queries, please contact your responsible Intermediaries Relationship Manager.

Licensing Department Intermediaries and Investment Products Division Securities and Futures Commission

1 'Intermediaries' means licensed corporations or registered institutions under the Securities and Futures Ordinance.

2 The FRR were amended by the Securities and Futures (Financial Resources) (Amendment) Rules 2006.
